# #90 — P1: Bind MCP sessions to delegated namespace identity

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-06-11T02:42:51Z
Updated: 2026-06-11T03:39:01Z
Closed: 2026-06-11T03:39:01Z

## Finding
MCP session reuse is bound to token identity and role, but not to the effective delegated namespace or agent id.

## Evidence
- `src/auth.ts:116` constructs request auth where `clientId` can be replaced by `X-Namespace`, while `tokenClientId` keeps the bearer token identity.
- `src/transport.ts:85` compares only `tokenClientId` and `role` in `sameTokenIdentity`.
- `src/transport.ts:115` reuses an existing session when `sameTokenIdentity` passes.
- `src/server.test.ts:188` explicitly asserts that the same token can initialize a session under `X-Namespace: bilby` and then reuse the same `Mcp-Session-Id` under `X-Namespace: skippy`.

## Risk
One MCP transport/server session can be reused across effective tenants. Even if individual tools read `extra.authInfo` per request, session-scoped MCP state, server-side resources, logs, and future tool/session assumptions become cross-namespace. This is especially risky for long-lived Python clients and delegated admin/n8n tokens.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bind MCP sessions to the effective namespace identity used at initialization, not just the token identity.
- Decide whether `X-Agent-Id` is also part of session identity; if it is not, document why and test the intended behavior.
- Replace the existing "allows same token session reuse with a different delegated namespace" test with a denial test.
- Cover POST, GET, and DELETE session reuse checks.
- Return a clear 403 error when the same `Mcp-Session-Id` is presented with a different effective namespace or bound agent identity.
